q: Only iodine forms hepta-fluoride IF7, but chlorine and bromine give penta-fluorides. The reason for this is
question: Only iodine forms hepta-fluoride IF7, but chlorine and bromine give penta-fluorides. The reason for this is
options: that the larger iodine atom can accommodate more number of smaller fluorine atom around it.
solution:
• Concept: The formation of interhalogen compounds ($XX'_n$) depends heavily on the ratio of the atomic radii of the central halogen ($X$) to the surrounding halogen ($X'$). As the size of the central atom increases relative to the surrounding atoms, it can coordinate with a greater number of them.

  • Application to $IF_7$: Iodine (I) is the largest atom among the common halogens, while fluorine (F) is the smallest. Because of its large atomic radius, iodine has sufficient spatial capacity to accommodate seven small fluorine atoms around it without experiencing severe steric hindrance (crowding).

  • Comparison with Cl and Br: Chlorine and bromine have significantly smaller atomic radii than iodine. They simply do not have enough surface area to fit seven fluorine atoms around them, capping their capacity at five (forming $ClF_5$ and $BrF_5$).

The correct statement is Option C: that the larger iodine atom can accommodate more number of smaller fluorine atom around it.

question: Heating of bleaching powder gives :
solution:
• Composition: Bleaching powder is a complex mixture, but its active constituent is often represented simply as $CaOCl_2$.

  • Reaction on Heating: When bleaching powder is heated, it undergoes auto-oxidation (a type of disproportionation reaction). The hypochlorite part disproportionates into chlorate and chloride ions.

  • Chemical Equation:

$$6CaOCl_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} Ca(ClO_3)_2 + 5CaCl_2$$

  • Products: The products formed are calcium chlorate [$Ca(ClO_3)_2$] and calcium chloride [$CaCl_2$].

Since both compounds are produced during the thermal decomposition of bleaching powder, the correct choice is Option D (both (a) and (b)).

question: The property of halogen acids, that indicated incorrect is
solution:
• Option A (Acidic strength): Acidic strength depends on the bond dissociation enthalpy of the H-X bond. As the size of the halogen atom increases down the group (from F to I), the H-X bond length increases and the bond becomes weaker. This makes it easier to release an $H^+$ ion. Therefore, the acidic strength increases down the group: HF < HCl < HBr < HI. The given order (HF > HCl > HBr > HI) is incorrect.

  • Option B (Reducing strength): Reducing character is linked to the ease of breaking the H-X bond to release hydrogen. Since the bond dissociation enthalpy decreases down the group, it becomes progressively easier to cleave the bond. Thus, reducing strength increases from HF to HI: HI > HBr > HCl > HF. This statement is correct.

  • Option C (Bond length): As we move down the halogen group, the atomic radius of the halogen increases significantly. Consequently, the distance between the hydrogen and halogen nuclei increases, making the bond longer: HI > HBr > HCl > HF. This statement is correct.

  • Option D (Thermal stability): Thermal stability is directly proportional to the bond dissociation enthalpy. Because the H-X bond strength decreases as the size of the halogen increases, less heat is required to break the bond. Therefore, thermal stability decreases down the group: HF > HCl > HBr > HI. This statement is correct.

The property that is indicated incorrectly is Option A.

question: Chlorine will oxidize Na2S2O3 to
solution:
• The Concept: The reaction of halogens with sodium thiosulphate ($\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}$) depends on the oxidizing power of the specific halogen used. This is a classic comparative reaction in NCERT:

  • Iodine ($I_2$) is a mild oxidizing agent. It oxidizes sodium thiosulphate only up to sodium tetrathionate ($\mathrm{Na_2S_4O_6}$).

Reaction: $2\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3} + I_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{Na_2S_4O_6} + 2NaI$

  • Chlorine ($Cl_2$) is a much stronger oxidizing agent. It completely oxidizes sodium thiosulphate to sodium sulphate ($\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}$), where sulfur reaches its highest oxidation state (+6).

  • The Chemical Equation:

$\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3} + 4Cl_2 + 5H_2O \rightarrow \mathrm{Na_2SO_4} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} + 8HCl$

Therefore, chlorine will oxidize $\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}$ to $\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}$.

The correct choice is Option A.

question: Halogens are colored due to
solution:
• NCERT Principle: All halogens are colored. This phenomenon occurs because their molecules absorb specific wavelengths of light from the visible region of the electromagnetic spectrum.

  • Mechanism of Color: The absorption of this visible light provides the energy required to excite the outer (valence) electrons to a higher energy level.

  • Molecular Orbital Context (Options Analysis):

  • In terms of molecular orbital theory, this excitation of outer electrons happens from the Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO) to the Lowest Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (LUMO).

  • Halogens exist as diatomic molecules ($X_2$) where electrons are paired, so it is not due to unpaired electrons (Option A).

  • They are p-block elements, so they do not undergo d-d transitions like transition metals (Option B).

  • The color is intrinsic to the molecule's electronic excitation, not an intermolecular charge transfer (Option D).

The correct option is Option C (HOMO–LUMO transition).

question: Choose the incorrect statement
options: Bromine can be prepared by oxidation of potassium bromide by chlorine.
Bromine is never found in free state.
Bromine can be prepared by action of hydrochloric acid on potassium bromide only.
Manufacturing of bromine is done using carnalite.
solution:
• Option A: Chlorine is a stronger oxidizing agent than bromine. Therefore, chlorine gas can easily oxidize bromide ions in an aqueous solution of potassium bromide to liberate free bromine ($2KBr + Cl_2 \rightarrow 2KCl + Br_2$). This statement is correct.

  • Option B: Halogens are highly reactive non-metals. Due to this high reactivity, they are never found in their free (elemental) state in nature, but rather as halides in various minerals and seawater. This statement is correct.

  • Option C: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is not a strong enough oxidizing agent to oxidize bromide ions ($Br^-$) to bromine ($Br_2$). To prepare bromine from potassium bromide, you need an oxidizing agent like chlorine gas, or manganese dioxide ($MnO_2$) in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid. Therefore, this statement is incorrect.

  • Option D: Carnallite ($KCl \cdot MgCl_2 \cdot 6H_2O$) deposits contain small amounts of bromides. During the processing of carnallite, the mother liquor left after the crystallization of chlorides is rich in bromide ions and is used industrially for the extraction/manufacturing of bromine. This statement is correct.

The incorrect statement is Option C.

(i) $OF_2$ (ii) $O_2$

question:
When $F_2$ reacts with hot and conc. alkali, then following will be obtained

(i) $OF_2$ (ii) $O_2$

(iii) $H_2O$ (iv) NaF
solution:
When fluorine ($F_2$) reacts with hot and concentrated alkali (such as NaOH), it produces oxygen gas ($O_2$), sodium fluoride (NaF), and water ($H_2O$).

The balanced chemical equation for this reaction is:

$$2F_2 + 4NaOH (hot\ and\ conc.) \rightarrow 4NaF + 2H_2O + O_2$$

(Note: If the alkali were cold and dilute, the reaction would produce $OF_2$ instead of $O_2$.)

Based on the products of the hot and concentrated reaction:

  • (ii) $O_2$ is obtained.

  • (iii) $H_2O$ is obtained.

  • (iv) NaF is obtained.

The correct choice is Option C: (ii), (iii) and (iv).

$$\mathrm{X + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Y + BaSO_4}$$

$$\mathrm{Y \xrightarrow[\Delta > 365\,K]{\Delta} Z + H_2O + HClO_4}$$

solution:
• Reaction 1: Chlorine with hot alkali

When chlorine gas reacts with a hot and concentrated alkali like barium hydroxide, it undergoes disproportionation to form barium chloride and barium chlorate.

$$6Cl_2 + 6Ba(OH)_2 \xrightarrow{Hot} Ba(ClO_3)_2(aq) + 5BaCl_2 + 6H_2O$$

Therefore, X is Barium chlorate [$Ba(ClO_3)_2$].

  • Reaction 2: Formation of Y

Reacting barium chlorate with sulfuric acid results in a double displacement reaction, yielding a precipitate of barium sulfate and a solution of chloric acid.

$$Ba(ClO_3)_2 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow 2HClO_3 + BaSO_4 \downarrow$$

Therefore, Y is Chloric acid [$HClO_3$].

  • Reaction 3: Thermal decomposition of Y

When chloric acid is heated above 365 K, it disproportionates into perchloric acid, chlorine dioxide, and water.

$$3HClO_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta > 365\,K} HClO_4 + 2ClO_2 + H_2O$$

Therefore, Z is Chlorine dioxide [$ClO_2$].

The compounds Y and Z are $HClO_3$ and $ClO_2$, respectively.

The correct choice is Option B.

Assertion (A) : HClO4 is a stronger acid than HClO3.

question:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : HClO4 is a stronger acid than HClO3.

Reason (R) : Oxidation state of chlorine in HClO4 is +7 and in HClO3 it is +5.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
solution:
• Assertion (A): $\text{HClO}_4$ is a stronger acid than $\text{HClO}_3$.

In the oxoacids of halogens, the acidic strength increases with the increase in the oxidation state of the central halogen atom. Because the central chlorine atom in $\text{HClO}_4$ is in a higher oxidation state, it has a stronger electron-withdrawing effect. This polarizes and weakens the O-H bond more effectively, making it easier to release an $\text{H}^+$ ion. Additionally, the conjugate base of $\text{HClO}_4$ ($\text{ClO}_4^-$) is more resonance-stabilized than the conjugate base of $\text{HClO}_3$ ($\text{ClO}_3^-$). Therefore, this statement is true.

  • Reason (R): Oxidation state of chlorine in $\text{HClO}_4$ is +7 and in $\text{HClO}_3$ it is +5.

  • In $\text{HClO}_4$: $(+1) + x + 4(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +7$

  • In $\text{HClO}_3$: $(+1) + x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +5$

This statement is factually true.

  • Connection:

The core reason why $\text{HClO}_4$ is a stronger acid than $\text{HClO}_3$ is precisely because of the higher oxidation state (+7 vs +5) of the central chlorine atom, which directly governs the electron-withdrawing capacity and conjugate base stability.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

The correct choice is Option A.

question:

(ii) $F_2$ is less reactive than $ClF$.

(iii) On hydrolysis $ClF$ form $HOCl$ and $HF$.

(iv) $F_2$ is a stronger oxidising agent than $Cl_2$ in aqueous.

(v) Fluorine forms two oxoacid due to small size and high electronegativity.
solution:
• (i) $Cl_2$ is less reactive than $ClF$: Interhalogen compounds are generally more reactive than halogens (except fluorine). This is because the $X-X'$ bond in interhalogens is weaker than the $X-X$ bond in halogens. Therefore, $ClF$ is more reactive than $Cl_2$. This statement is correct.

  • (ii) $F_2$ is less reactive than $ClF$: Fluorine is an exception to the general reactivity rule of interhalogens. The $F-F$ bond is exceptionally weak due to high interelectronic repulsions between the small, lone-pair-rich fluorine atoms. Thus, $F_2$ is much more reactive than $ClF$. This statement is incorrect.

  • (iii) On hydrolysis $ClF$ form $HOCl$ and $HF$: When interhalogen compounds undergo hydrolysis, the smaller, more electronegative halogen forms the halide ion (or hydrohalic acid), and the larger halogen forms the oxoacid. For $ClF$, fluorine forms $HF$ and chlorine forms hypochlorous acid ($HOCl$). This statement is correct.

  • (iv) $F_2$ is a stronger oxidising agent than $Cl_2$ in aqueous: Fluorine is the strongest oxidizing agent among the halogens. This is due to its low bond dissociation enthalpy, high electron gain enthalpy, and the exceptionally high hydration enthalpy of the small $F^-$ ion in aqueous solutions. This statement is correct.

  • (v) Fluorine forms two oxoacid due to small size and high electronegativity: Due to its very small size and extremely high electronegativity, fluorine does not form multiple oxoacids. It forms only one oxoacid, hypofluorous acid ($HOF$). This statement is incorrect.

The incorrect statements are (ii) and (v).

Therefore, the total number of incorrect statements is 2.

q:
The total number of colored species among the following is $\_\_\_\_$.

$\mathrm{ClF}, \mathrm{ClF}_3, \mathrm{BrF}, \mathrm{BrF}_3, \mathrm{BrF}_5, \mathrm{ClF}_5, \mathrm{IF}_3, \mathrm{IF}_5, \mathrm{IF}_7$
question:
The total number of colored species among the following is $\_\_\_\_$.

$\mathrm{ClF}, \mathrm{ClF}_3, \mathrm{BrF}, \mathrm{BrF}_3, \mathrm{BrF}_5, \mathrm{ClF}_5, \mathrm{IF}_3, \mathrm{IF}_5, \mathrm{IF}_7$
solution:
The general rule for the color of interhalogen compounds is:

  1. All interhalogen compounds with chlorine as the central atom are colorless.

  2. Interhalogen compounds having bromine or iodine as the central atom are colored, with the exception of $\mathrm{BrF}_5, \mathrm{IF}_5$, and $\mathrm{IF}_7$, which are colorless.

Applying this rule to the given species:

  • Colorless (Chlorine as central atom): $\mathrm{ClF}, \mathrm{ClF}_3, \mathrm{ClF}_5$

  • Colorless (Exceptions): $\mathrm{BrF}_5, \mathrm{IF}_5, \mathrm{IF}_7$

  • Colored (Bromine or Iodine as central atom): $\mathrm{BrF}, \mathrm{BrF}_3, \mathrm{IF}_3$

The colored species are exactly $\mathrm{BrF}$, $\mathrm{BrF}_3$, and $\mathrm{IF}_3$.

Total number of colored species = 3.
explanation:
The general rule for the color of interhalogen compounds is:

  1. All interhalogen compounds with chlorine as the central atom are colorless.

  2. Interhalogen compounds having bromine or iodine as the central atom are colored, with the exception of $\mathrm{BrF}_5, \mathrm{IF}_5$, and $\mathrm{IF}_7$, which are colorless.

Applying this rule to the given species:

  • Colorless (Chlorine as central atom): $\mathrm{ClF}, \mathrm{ClF}_3, \mathrm{ClF}_5$

  • Colorless (Exceptions): $\mathrm{BrF}_5, \mathrm{IF}_5, \mathrm{IF}_7$

  • Colored (Bromine or Iodine as central atom): $\mathrm{BrF}, \mathrm{BrF}_3, \mathrm{IF}_3$

The colored species are exactly $\mathrm{BrF}$, $\mathrm{BrF}_3$, and $\mathrm{IF}_3$.

Total number of colored species = 3.

Hydrochloric acid is formed by the hydrolysis of how many of the following species?

$\mathrm{PCl}}_{3}, $\mathrm{AgCl}, \mathrm{SiCl}}_{4}, $\mathrm{NCl}}_{3}, $\mathrm{ClF}}_{3}, $\mathrm{ClF}}_{5}

question:
Hydrochloric acid is formed by the hydrolysis of how many of the following species?

$\mathrm{PCl}}_{3}, $\mathrm{AgCl}, \mathrm{SiCl}}_{4}, $\mathrm{NCl}}_{3}, $\mathrm{ClF}}_{3}, $\mathrm{ClF}}_{5}

$
solution:
• $\mathrm{PCl}_3$: Undergoes hydrolysis to form phosphorous acid and hydrochloric acid.

$$\mathrm{PCl}_3 + 3\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{H_3PO_3} + 3\mathrm{HCl}$$

(Forms $\mathrm{HCl}$)

  • $\mathrm{AgCl}$: This is an insoluble ionic salt and does not undergo hydrolysis in water.

(Does not form $\mathrm{HCl}$)

  • $\mathrm{SiCl}_4$: Undergoes complete hydrolysis to form silicic acid and hydrochloric acid.

$$\mathrm{SiCl}_4 + 4\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{Si(OH)_4} + 4\mathrm{HCl}$$

(Forms $\mathrm{HCl}$)

  • $\mathrm{NCl}_3$: During hydrolysis, water attacks the vacant d-orbitals of the chlorine atoms, resulting in the formation of ammonia and hypochlorous acid ($\mathrm{HOCl}$).

$$\mathrm{NCl}_3 + 3\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{NH_3} + 3\mathrm{HOCl}$$

(Does not form $\mathrm{HCl}$)

  • $\mathrm{ClF}_3$ & $\mathrm{ClF}_5$: When interhalogen compounds undergo hydrolysis, the smaller, more electronegative halogen (fluorine) forms the hydrohalic acid ($\mathrm{HF}$), while the central halogen (chlorine) forms the corresponding oxoacid.
$\mathrm{ClF}_5+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{FClO}_2+4 \mathrm{HF}$

(They form $\mathrm{HF}$, not $\mathrm{HCl}$)

The species that form hydrochloric acid upon hydrolysis are exactly two: $\mathrm{PCl}_3$ and $\mathrm{SiCl}_4$.

The correct integer answer is 2.

q:
When diatomic molecule of chlorine react with hot and concentrated NaOH the oxidation state of chlorine in reactant i.e., $(O)$ is changed to $x$ and $y$ in formed product.

The value of $x+y$ is $\_\_\_\_$
question:
When diatomic molecule of chlorine react with hot and concentrated NaOH the oxidation state of chlorine in reactant i.e., $(O)$ is changed to $x$ and $y$ in formed product.

The value of $x+y$ is $\_\_\_\_$
solution:
• The Reaction: When chlorine gas ($\text{Cl}_2$) reacts with hot and concentrated sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$), it undergoes a disproportionation reaction to form sodium chloride ($\text{NaCl}$) and sodium chlorate ($\text{NaClO}_3$), along with water.

$$3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{NaOH} (\text{hot and conc.}) \rightarrow 5\text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2O$$

  • Oxidation States:

  • In the reactant $\text{Cl}_2$, the oxidation state of chlorine is $0$.

  • In the product $\text{NaCl}$, the oxidation state of chlorine ($x$) is $-1$.

  • In the product $\text{NaClO}_3$, the oxidation state of chlorine ($y$) is $+5$ (since $+1 + y + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow y = +5$).

  • Calculation:

The question asks for the value of $x + y$:

$$x + y = (-1) + (+5) = 4$$

The value of $x + y$ is 4.
